audio: Plays an audio file into the patch: crop it, loop it, set its gain. Most chains start here.
Drop a file on the canvas to make one.
generator: Makes noise: white, pink, brown, blue, violet, dust (sparse random clicks) and more, at a set Length and Level, mono or stereo.
Dust into a Resonator gives tuned plucks.
preview: Renders the chain up to this point and plays it, so you can listen anywhere without baking a file.
print: Writes what reaches it to a WAV file: 16-bit, 24-bit or 32-bit float, optionally with a wavetable chunk for Serum or Vital, and optional Clean Up (trim silence, fades, remove DC, normalize).
Set Bit Depth to 32-bit float when the file is going back into BAKE or into a wavetable synth.
batchAudio: Plays a folder of audio files, one file per pass of a batch. Everything after it runs once for each file.
Batch Audio → Filters → Batch Bake processes a whole folder.
largeAudio: Cuts one long recording into slices (at transients, by musical length, or every few seconds) and plays one slice per pass.
A long jam → Large Audio Processor → Batch Bake gives a folder of one-shots.
photoBooth: Takes a snapshot of its input at every trigger (a Clock, LFO, Logic…, or every 1/4 at its own BPM when nothing is wired). Each chunk becomes a pass of the batch.
Audio (a groove) → Photo Booth → Batch Bake gives groove-001, groove-002 and so on.
concatenate: Joins its inputs end to end (In 1, then In 2, …), with gaps or crossfades. In a batch it also joins every pass: each file's inputs in order, then the next file's. What comes after it runs once, on the joined result.
Three Audio nodes into In 1, In 2 and In 3 make one file; after a Batch Audio, wire the file into In 1 and a Reverse of it into In 2 for each sound then its reverse.
corpusScatter: Scatters every pass of a batch along one timeline (random, even or Euclidean timing), with pitch and pan variation. The same Seed gives the same result.
A folder of short hits with Density 20 makes a texture; Euclidean timing makes a groove.
ensembleAverager: Averages the spectra of every pass of a batch into one sound: 200 snares in, one composite snare out. Mean, Median or Geometric; lined up by Start, Onset or Peak.
For drums, Onset alignment with FFT Size 1024–2048. For very mixed folders, Median.
combinatorialMatrix: Layers inputs A, B and C. In a batch, every combination of the files on A, B and C becomes its own pass: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1 000 files.
Clicks on A and subs on B → Batch Bake gives click03+sub07.wav and so on.
forEachSplitter: Sends each file of a batch down one or more of its outputs: Broadcast, Round-Robin, Odd/Even or Blocks. A Batch Bake behind an output writes only the files sent its way.
spectralSorter: Measures each clip (brightness, loudness, pitch or decay) and sends it to Low, Mid or High. With a Batch Bake on each output, a folder sorts itself into three.
A drum folder by Centroid separates kicks, snares and hats.
merryGoRound: Deals each file of a batch to one output in turn: Forward, Ping-Pong, Random or a typed Pattern, Hold files at a time.
After a Large Audio Processor, Hold 4 keeps runs of consecutive slices together.
batchConform: Stretches and repitches every file to a Target BPM and Key. It reads the tempo and key from the file name when it can (128bpm, Am), otherwise it detects them.
Formants on Preserve for vocals and solo instruments; Shift for everything else.
batchBake: Writes one file per pass of a batch, named after the source, numbered (Kick_001), or with random words. Clean Up is optional.
filters: A resonant filter: low-pass, high-pass, band-pass or notch, with Drive and slopes up to 96 dB/oct, in Minimum (IIR) or Linear (FIR) phase.
dualFilter: Two filters, Alpha and Beta, with Spread between their cutoffs, Morph between them, and a built-in LFO.
resonator: A bank of tuned resonant bands that rings at a Root pitch and its partials; Inharmonicity bends them toward bells and metal. Runs on the GPU.
Dust from a Generator into a Resonator gives plucked, tuned sounds.
distortion: Soft or hard clipping with Drive, Ceiling and Mix, oversampled to keep it clean.
redux: Lo-fi degradation: bit reduction, downsampling, sample-and-hold and bitwise modes.
waveshaper: Bends the waveform through a curve (tanh, arctan, sine, Chebyshev, asymmetric and more), with Drive and Bias.
wavefolder: Folds the waveform back on itself as it gets louder, for rich, buzzy harmonics: triangle or sine folds, up to 8 stages.
derivativeDistortion: Distorts a sound's movement rather than its peaks, by limiting how fast and how sharply the waveform can change.
residualExplosion: Simplifies the sound (fewer bits, or quiet samples removed) and turns up what was thrown away; Body blends the original back in. Runs on the GPU.
subHarmonic: Adds tones one and two octaves below the pitch it tracks, for weight under basses and kicks.
tapeDegrade: Wow, flutter, saturation, hiss and dropouts, like a worn tape machine.
adaptiveClipping: A clipper that holds peaks at its Threshold and lets go smoothly, with a hard or soft knee, look-ahead and makeup gain.
compressor: Compressor, expander or gate, with a sidechain input, peak or RMS detection, stereo or mid/side linking and sidechain filters.
limiter: A look-ahead limiter that keeps peaks under the Ceiling, oversampled to catch peaks between samples.
phaser: A sweeping phaser with its own LFO: Center, Width, Rate, Depth and Feedback, 2–24 stages.
flanger: A short modulated delay with feedback, for jet-plane sweeps.
chorus: Several detuned, delayed voices for width and shimmer: Detune, Spread, 2–8 voices.
frequencyShifter: Shifts every frequency up or down by the same number of hertz (not a pitch shift), for metallic and detuned sounds. Up and Down have their own outputs.
delay: Echoes with Feedback, Damping, Ping-Pong, several Taps, Pitch per Repeat and Freeze.
convolver: Puts a sound in the space (or texture) of another: wire an impulse response into IR, or leave IR empty to convolve the sound with itself.
Audio → Convolver ← Batch Audio (on IR) → Batch Bake convolves one sound with every file in a folder.
reverb: A feedback-delay-network reverb: Size, Decay, Damping, Diffusion, separate low and high decay, and Freeze.
granularCloud: Chops the input into tiny grains and sprays them into a cloud: Grain Size, Density, Spray, pitch and stereo spread, reverse chance.
temporalShatter: Keeps each attack as it is and stretches what follows, by huge factors if you like, as grains or as tape.
halfTime: Slows the sound to half speed or less, as tape (repitched) or keeping pitch (granular). Modulate Speed for tape stops.
beatRepeat: Ableton-style beat repeat with its own tempo: grabs a slice and repeats it, down to buzzy 1/2048 grids, with pitch, decay and chance.
looper: Loops a slice of the input at each bang (or every few ms) until the next one.
A Clock on Trigger loops a fresh slice every beat.
stutter: Micro-repeats on each bang (or every few ms): Size, Repeats, Shrink, Decay, pitch and pan drift, Reverse.
stepFX: A step sequencer of effects, Effectrix-style: each step is Pass, Stutter, Reverse, Tape Stop, Half Time or Gate. Click the card's cells to edit.
stretch: Time-stretches without changing pitch, or shifts pitch without changing length, up to 1000×.
reverse: Plays the sound backwards, with Mix.
vocoder: A channel vocoder: the modulator's spectrum shapes the carrier, with Bands, Formant Shift, Attack and Release.
spectralResynthesis: Rebuilds the sound from its partials (sines plus noise): tilt, pitch, stretch, crystallize. With a second input: cross-synthesis, morph, splice or swap noise.
fractalFilter: Carves a self-similar spectral mask (Cantor, Mandelbrot, Julia, Koch and more) into the sound. Runs on the GPU.
otftCompressor: Over-the-top spectral compression: every frequency bin gets its own upward and downward compressor, for extreme flattening and detail.
singleCycle: Generates single-cycle waveforms (Wavetable mode) or a playable oscillator, from shapes and harmonics with Warp and Morph.
Single Cycle → effects → Wavetable Factory → Bake makes a wavetable for Serum or Vital.
wavetableFactory: Builds a wavetable from the cycles fed into it; Bake writes it in a form Serum and Vital read.
mixer: Mixes any number of inputs (they grow as you wire, up to 16) with a master Gain.
gainVCA: Gain in dB; wire a control into Amount for tremolo (VCA) or ring modulation.
utility: The handy box: gain, balance, polarity, mono, fades, DC removal, normalize, and trimming or padding either end.
stepSwitch: Sends the audio to the next of its 2–8 outputs at each bang on Advance, with short crossfades: forward, ping-pong, random or a typed pattern.
channelSplitter: Splits a multichannel signal into mono outputs, one per channel.
channelMerger: Merges mono inputs into one multichannel signal.
frequencySplitter: Splits the sound into 2–5 frequency bands, each on its own output.
Process the lows and highs differently, then bring them back with a Mixer.
midSideEncoder: Turns left and right into Mid (the centre) and Side (the width).
midSideDecoder: Turns Mid and Side back into left and right.
feedback: Feeds a chain's output back into its input, with Delay, Drive and always-on saturation, so loops stay safe.
Select a chain and use Make Feedback Group (⌥⌘G).
lfo: A low-frequency oscillator: sine, triangle, saw, square or sample-and-hold, free-running or synced to a Clock.
random: Random values over time (stepped, smooth, or a random walk), uniform, Gaussian or coin-flip, at a Rate or on each trigger.
sampleAndHold: Samples a signal at each trigger (or at a Rate) and holds it, with glide.
macro: One dial that drives many controls at once, each with its own depth, curve and range. Inside a Custom Node it becomes a control on the card.
envelope: An ADSR envelope fired by bangs (or every few ms): one-shot, gate or classic.
envelopeFollower: Turns the loudness of an audio signal into a control signal, with Attack and Release.
pitchFollower: Tracks the pitch of an audio signal as a control, with a Confidence output that works as a gate.
transientDetector: Sends a bang at every hit in an audio signal, plus how strong it was: energy, spectral flux or high-frequency detection.
featureFollower: Follows a spectral feature (brightness, noisiness, flux, rolloff, bandwidth or zero crossings) as a control signal.
clock: Sends bangs at a BPM and division (1/1–1/64, dotted, triplet). It drives LFOs, envelopes, Switch, Stutter, Photo Booth and more.
math: Combines two controls: add, subtract, multiply, divide, absolute, invert or modulo, with Scale and clamping.
logic: Turns controls into 0 or 1: threshold, AND, OR, XOR or NOT, with hysteresis and hold.
quantizer: Snaps a control to the notes of a scale (chromatic, major, minor, pentatonic) from a Root, with glide.
